notes: Claims are in first-pass ledger order (sections, faqs, keyFacts). Items marked 'not re-retrieved verbatim' (prescription-only, angina/AF uses, 'works as well', sit/lie down) were consistent with NHS page titles and retrieved text but I did not see the exact sentences; they were kept as supported on the strength of the NHS pages and the first-pass quotes. ASTHMA: the retrieved NHS who-can-and-cannot page lists 'lung disease or severe asthma' as a caution, and the leaflets list severe asthma as a reason not to take it; the article therefore says 'lung disease or severe asthma' and does not say asthma is generally excluded. This is softer than the existing record ('avoided in asthma'); a reviewer should reconcile. Removed: 'after eating might help' (NHS says with or without food), sleep disturbance 'common' (leaflet says less common/rare), amitriptyline by name, clinical shock/antiarrhythmics, NHS-linked asthma-worse claim, slow-heart-rate sentence, alcohol BP-mechanism, 'started and reviewed by a prescriber'. Added from retrieved text: BHF selectivity and mechanism, NHS stopping/BP rise, NHS interaction groups, NHS pregnancy-page growth/scans, NHS 999 allergic-reaction wording. Reference URLs: emc URL changed to pil.13703.pdf (the leaflet actually retrieved); beta-blockers NHS page dropped (not relied on). Length: sections total about 750 words; whole article including FAQs and key facts about 1,170 words, so over 900 if the cap applies to everything.
